$comment: Hand-written expected values for fixtures/specs/unicode-text.json (criterion 33; also 13 and 14 through it). Bidi controls and U+2028 are written here as \u escapes so this file is readable; the fixture holds them as raw UTF-8 (see 'controls'). Request entries use the comparison form of fixtures/specs/expected/request-shape-matrix.json and ADR 0005 'How a received request is compared'. Percent-escapes were worked out from ADR 0005 'Text outside ASCII' rule 1 (UTF-8 bytes, upper-case hex, space %20; path template literal text: each code point that is not an RFC 3986 pchar or '/' encoded) and cross-checked with Python's urllib.parse.quote. Ids and slugs are from ADR 0002 'Identifiers' and contract 1.1, worked by hand.

controls.rule: Criterion 33's list. Every occurrence in the fixture of U+061C, U+200E, U+200F, U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069, U+2028 or U+2029 (ADR 0005 rule 3(b)) is one of these, and each of these is present. The tag name with U+202E is also each operation's 'tags' entry that names it.

occurrences.what: that tag name, used by an operation
that tag name, used by an operation
that tag name, used by an operation
an operation summary, unclosed (no U+2069 follows)
inside a right-to-left (Hebrew) sentence with the Latin word API and the number 2

scripts.rule: Criterion 33: the fixture as a whole holds each of these. The integrity test checks each by code point range.
required: a non-BMP character that is not an emoji (U+2000B)
one string in NFD that differs from its NFC

nfd.rule: A schema name in NFD ('e' + U+0301). Kept as authored (ADR 0002 'Text is kept as authored'); its slug is 'cafe', where NFC would give 'caf'.

operationsRule: Criterion 33(d); contract 1.1 and ADR 0002 'Identifiers'. A declared operationId is used verbatim. A derived id is the method and the path with each code point (not UTF-16 code unit) outside A-Za-z0-9 replaced by one '_': 'post' + '/' + 8 Arabic letters gives 'post' and 9 underscores; 'get' + '/' + U+1F389 gives 'get__'. A slug keeps ASCII a-z0-9 runs joined by '-', so an id with none gets 'x'; in the operations pool three ids get 'x', taken in code point order of the id: U+0928 (Devanagari) 'x', U+691C (検) 'x-2', U+83B7 (获) 'x-3'. 'post_________' and 'get__' become 'post' and 'get' once '-' runs are trimmed.
tagsRule: ADR 0002 Slug, tags pool: U+0645 (Arabic) sorts before U+30E6 (Katakana), so the Arabic tag keeps 'x' and the Japanese one gets 'x-2'. The U+202E tag keeps only its ASCII run 'invoices' (lower-cased)
schemasRule: ADR 0002 Slug, schemas pool: U+0645 (Arabic) before U+0909 (Devanagari). Fragments are 'schema-' + slug (ADR 0003 'Fragments'), all ASCII.

lengths.rule: Criterion 33(e); ADR 0003 'Schema validation': minLength and maxLength count code points. U+1F389 is one code point and two UTF-16 code units.

requests.rule: ADR 0005 rule 1: the template's literal text and the path value, UTF-8, upper-case hex

ADR 0005 rule 1: names and values encoded, space %20 (the ADR's own example value). Only required parameters are sent (ADR 0005 'Rules'); the sort parameter takes its first enum value. Declared order is also code point order (question QA-2)
ADR 0005 'How a received request is compared': JSON compared parsed, strings by code point after escapes are decoded, so U+202E and U+2028 match although samples write them as \u escapes (rule 3(b))
ADR 0005 rule 1: a form field name and value are encoded like a query's; 'city' sorts before the Arabic name by code point and is first in the schema and the example

Criterion 33(i); ADR 0005 rule 2: a header value that is not printable ASCII is left out with request-invalid; the mock answers 400 because a required parameter is missing, and the request is still compared
Criterion 33(i); ADR 0005 rule 2 and 'Cookies': a non-ASCII cookie value is refused, so no Cookie header at all; the mock answers 400

Criterion 33(i); ADR 0005 rule 2: a part whose name is not printable ASCII, and one whose name holds '=', are left out; part content is UTF-8 and is sent. The mock validates JSON bodies only (ADR 0005 'It accepts a request'), so it answers 200

includes.rule: ADR 0002 Slug: '検索する' takes 'x-2'. Reported at the item that did not keep the slug (question QA-9)
ADR 0002 Slug: tag 'ユーザー' takes 'x-2'

findings.exactCodesRule: Criterion 33(e) for example-invalid. Criterion 33(i): exactly one request-invalid for each refused header, cookie and part. ADR 0004 gives request-invalid no location; the parameter declaration is asserted for the header and cookie with the operation accepted (question QA-10), and the parts' pointers are not asserted, only their count. No id collides, so no operation-id-collision (contract 1.1).
